name: Treaty with the Delawares, etc., 1809 (Treaty of Fort Wayne)
aka: Treaty with the Delawares, Potawatomi, Miami and Eel River, 1809
nations: Wea (now part of the Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma)
promises: Permanent annuities for the cession: $500 each to the Delawares, Miami and Potawatomi, and $250 to the Eel River (Article 3), with $5,200 in goods delivered (Article 6).
The Treaty of Greenville's terms on annuity payment and the Indians' right to hunt on ceded land would apply (Article 4).
The Wea's consent was needed to complete the title, with goods and a permanent annuity of at least $300 to be settled on them (Article 5).
The Miami acknowledged the Delawares' equal right to the White River country, which neither could sell without the other's consent (Article 2).

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission found that the United States paid the Miami and Eel River $18,728 in all for their interests in Royce Areas 71 and 72 ceded by this treaty: $13,764.80 for their part of Area 71 and $4,875 for Area 72 (the Twelve-mile Strip). It valued their part of Area 71 at $1,933,300 and Area 72 at $850,000 on 16 January 1810, held both considerations unconscionable, and awarded $1,919,535.20 and $845,125.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Indian Claims Commission, Miami Tribe of Oklahoma et al. v. United States, Dockets 253 and 131, Additional Findings and Conclusions of 26 November 1969 (22 Ind. Cl. Comm. 92)

source.title: Miami Tribe of Oklahoma v. United States, Dockets 253, 131 and 314-D, Additional Findings of Fact on Value and Conclusions (1969)
source.publisher: Oklahoma State University Library, Indian Claims Commission Decisions

landTaken: Area 71 ceded by this treaty and the Wea convention of 26 October 1809 contained 2,095,688 acres; Area 72, the Twelve-mile Strip, 547,630 acres (Docket 253 findings, 1969). The Commission also found settlers on Area 72 as early as 1803 and 1804, before it was ceded.
compensation: Annuities and goods valued by the Commission at $18,728 for the Miami and Eel River interests in Areas 71 and 72, and $7,500 for the Wea interest in Area 71. Awards of $1,919,535.20 and $845,125 (Miami and Eel River) and $678,900 (Wea) in 1969.
today: The Delaware and Potawatomi interests in this cession were not part of these dockets.

nationVoice.nation: Myaamia (Miami Tribe of Oklahoma), through the Myaamia Center's community blog
nationVoice.summary: A Myaamia Center history says Mihšihkinaahkwa (Little Turtle) was removed from civil leadership after the Treaty of Fort Wayne because most Myaamia held that the ceded lands belonged to the Miami Nation alone and that the Delaware and Potawatomi he brought into the talks should not benefit from their sale.

openQuestions: Whether Delaware or Potawatomi claims for this cession were heard by the Commission was not traced.
A Miami Tribe of Oklahoma statement on this treaty was not found; the Myaamia Center's Aacimotaatiiyankwi blog may have one.
Royce Area 73 (Article 9, the cession for the Kickapoo) is recorded under kappler-111 and kappler-112.

Audit 2026-11-08: removed 'under a cent an acre' and 'about 2.09 million acres' from the first breach, which were the researcher's own arithmetic; replaced with the per-area payments the Commission states ($13,764.80 and $4,875) per 22 Ind. Cl. Comm. 92, pp. 177-178.

Audit 2026-11-08 (round 11): moved here from kappler-111 (now the Wea convention only). Area 73 (Article 9 strip, 405,000 acres): the Indian Claims Commission found it worth $1.40 an acre on March 5, 1810, the Wea paid a $100 annuity commuted at $2,000, and held the consideration for Areas 73 and 74 unconscionable (Peoria Tribe v. United States, Dockets 99, 314-C and 317, Supplemental Findings of December 5, 1969, 22 Ind. Cl. Comm. 186, https://cdm17279.contentdm.oclc.org/digital/collection/p17279coll10/id/2276; Docket 314-C final award $349,750, January 1970, https://cdm17279.contentdm.oclc.org/digital/collection/p17279coll10/id/1048). Not yet added here as a breach; a researcher should decide whether it belongs on this record or on kappler-112 (the Kickapoo consent).

Audit 2026-11-08 (round 11): this file's second breach (Wea, 549,081 acres in Area 71, $7,500, $678,900) is the Wea's relinquishment under the convention of October 26, 1809: the Commission's finding 64 (22 Ind. Cl. Comm. 92, OSU id 2096) ties the $7,500 to that treaty, and kappler-111 now carries it. Counting it here as well double counts; a researcher or auditor of this file should remove it.

2026-11-08: the Wea Area 71 award ($678,900) was removed here because the Commission ties it to the Wea convention of Oct 26, 1809, now recorded on kappler-111. Whether the Area 73 finding (Docket 314-C) belongs here or on kappler-112 is still open.

plain.promised: In return for land in Indiana, the United States promised permanent yearly payments of $500 each to the Delawares, Miami and Potawatomi and $250 to the Eel River, $5,200 in goods, and hunting rights on the ceded land.
plain.happened: The Indian Claims Commission found in 1969 that the Miami and Eel River were paid $18,728 for land it valued at $1,933,300 and $850,000, and held these payments unconscionable.
plain.today: The Commission awarded $1,919,535.20 and $845,125 to the Miami and Eel River in 1969. The Wea share is on the Wea convention of October 26, 1809. Whether the awards were paid has not been traced.
